question: Should OpenClaw adopt this reusable core publisher-feed verification foundation before the referenced ClawHub producer protocol and RFC are finalized?
rationale: The patch is a new cross-repository trust and feature boundary, not a narrowly established bug fix; only maintainers can decide whether this capability belongs in core now and which compatibility contract OpenClaw will support.

options.title: Approve the core foundation with proof
options.body: Confirm the core ownership and accepted DSSE/publisher-feed contract, then require redacted producer-output proof before merge.

options.title: Defer until protocol settlement
options.body: Pause this foundation until the RFC and ClawHub producer format are finalized, then rebase a narrower implementation onto the accepted contract.

recommendation.title: Approve the core foundation with proof
recommendation.body: Confirm the core ownership and accepted DSSE/publisher-feed contract, then require redacted producer-output proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete technical owner signal in the linked publisher-feed series and can supply the requested producer proof; a repository maintainer must make the product decision.
